question: I live in the Fens. Which matters more for the climate here: the drained peat fields, the cattle and sheep, or the trees in hedges and around farms? What could change it?

assumptions.assumption: 'The Fens' is represented by the DT6 'fens' pilot tile (5 km) and, for livestock, a 10 km radius circle around the same area; drained peat fluxes use DT8's East Anglian Fens calibration.
assumptions.rationale: No specific location given; these are the agents' Fenland representations.

assumptions.assumption: Drained peat fields represented by winter wheat, sugar beet and potato under the default Fenland water table (~0.66 m), typical rates of fertiliser.

Compare on a per-hectare / per-km² of land basis and as totals over the same area, in t CO2e/yr using AR6 GWP100 where possible (DT8 uses AR6; DT2 gives AR6). Tree carbon is a stock plus an annual net uptake flux.
assumptions.rationale: Allows like-for-like comparison of the three sources.

assumptions.assumption: Levers examined: raising the water table (rewetting, reed/paludiculture), herd change/feed additive for livestock, and new hedgerow tree planting (1,000 trees) for TOW.
assumptions.rationale: Main levers each agent can model.

assumptions.assumption: Feed additive giving a herd-average 20 % enteric CH4 reduction for dairy and beef/other cattle, and separately a 25 % cut in cattle and sheep numbers, over the 5 km Fens tile.
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative sizes for the main livestock levers.

assumptions.assumption: 1,000 new hedgerow trees planted in 2025 in the Fens pilot, followed for 30 years.
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative scale: roughly 40 % more trees than the tile's 2,379.

assumptions.assumption: DT2/Living England shows 1,590 ha of arable in the tile, but no agent maps peat depth or extent. Totals for peat are given per hectare, plus an illustrative 'break-even' area and a hypothetical upper bound if all that arable were drained peat.
assumptions.rationale: Peat area is not available from the agents.

assumptions: Inventory: National Trees Outside Woodland map V1 (lone trees, groups of trees, small woodlands; canopy > 3 m outside NFI woodland). NFI overhanging canopy is left to DT4, hedges below 3 m to DT5.
Calibrated on Environment Agency lidar canopy heights only: first and last return of the National LIDAR Programme and last-return LIDAR Tiles DSMs back to 1998, all above the NLP terrain model.
Biomass from crown size and height with Jucker et al. (2017); trees in groups share the object's crown area equally; leaf type is a pilot prior (no open leaf-type map for TOW).
Crown light-use model climate: HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 monthly averages; radiation from Hargreaves-Samani.
Trees removed before the TOW map was made (2016-2023 lidar) are not in the inventory, so their loss is not seen.
